# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 35 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_035_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Chapter 1 — The Two Angels

**1** "I commanded you," he said, "in my first commandment to guard faith and fear and self-control." "Yes, sir," I said. **2** "But now," he said, "I want to show you the powers of these, so that you may understand what each one is and how it works. **3** Their powers are twofold, and they relate equally to the righteous and the unrighteous." **4** "How so, sir?" I said. "Listen," he said. "The righteous man has faith and fear and self-control. Now among the righteous there are two angels dwelling — one of righteousness and one of wickedness." **5** "Then how will I know their operations, sir?" I said, "since both angels dwell with me?" **6** "Listen and understand," he said. "The angel of righteousness is sensitive and modest and gentle and peaceful. When therefore this one enters your heart, immediately it speaks to you of righteousness, of purity, of holiness, of contentment, of every righteous deed, and of all glorious virtues. When all these things enter your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. **7** These are the works of the angel of righteousness. Trust him, therefore, and his works. **8** Now see also the works of the angel of wickedness. First of all, he is bitter and wrathful and senseless, and his works are evil, casting down the servants of God. Whenever therefore this one enters your heart, know him from his works. **9** He engenders in you anger and bitterness and folly and every kind of wickedness. When therefore these arise in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is in you. And you, knowing his works, keep your distance from him and trust him in nothing."

---

*EMET note: Mandate 6.1 — the Two Angels doctrine. Every person has two angels — one of righteousness, one of wickedness. This is a notable angelological doctrine, paralleled in the Qumran Two Spirits teaching (1QS 3:13-4:26). Identification by their works rather than direct perception.*
